sf_e9.text: Wall time per simulated hour against sites × LLMs (one day per run; medians over 4 alignments at policy seed 0, with the range over the alignments as bars and, for the LP, as a grey band; invariant checks on; the host's 1-min load average at a job's start: median 1.42, at most 4.00). The points are, from left to right, $V$ = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 and 64 layers per trace lender. (a) The full menu of E7 (20 revocable contracts) and (b) the reduced menu (3): the slow loop (lines with markers) and the fast loop (lines with small markers) of each policy; the setup per run (build, inputs, construction and reset) is left out and given in Table~\ref{tab:e9-steps}. (b) also gives the time to build and solve the LP bound over the day, divided by its simulated hours (black dashed; the merged relaxation on the slow grid). (a) has no LP bound: on the full menu the LP's estimated memory, at least 4.8 GB, exceeds the 3 GB cap of a job. (c) The slow-step P99 on the full menu. Grey: real time (3,600 s per simulated hour) and the 5-min slow slot. The two fast loops cross between $V$ = 16 and 32 and differ by at most 31% from $V$ = 16 on; where they meet, the line of Lagged RetroRenting + one-way guard ($B_0=10\%$ of the all-fallback bill), drawn last, covers the other. At $V$ = 32 and 64 the LP of alignment 2 was not solved in E9's run, since its estimated memory exceeded the LP runs' gate of 2,800 MB; it was solved separately on the same instance and is included in the median and range.

sf_s1.text: The saving over all-fallback of Lagged RetroRenting + one-way guard ($B_0=10\%$ of the all-fallback bill) in overflow accounting per assumption on E7's main week (one week; medians over 4 alignments × 3 policy seeds; each setting's saving over its own all-fallback cost). A bar runs from the lowest to the highest median over the row's settings (markers) and the default (grey line, 28.4%), labeled with the settings at its ends; rows sorted by span. $\Gamma$ is re-solved to keep the market tightness at its default 0.5 (in its own row, at the row's values) in every row of (b) and in the lease quantile, offered layers $V_\ell$, layer GPUs and buffer quantile rows of (c). Its allowance $B_0$ is 10\% of each run's all-fallback cost. The $\alpha_p$ and protected term rows change nothing: the policy leases no protected capacity at their settings. L-rf refuses purchases on unavailable layers, L-vr turns buffer violations into reclaims without notice (off: the default lender; on: the variant); no buffer violation occurred in its L-vr runs, so they equal the default lender's. The $\mu/\tilde{\beta}$ row reuses E7's runs. Bar ends not labeled: Load scenario from WAN 1 Gb/s to warm peer (Table~\ref{tab:s1-points}). Not run: the warm-peer and SSD load-rate scaling, the client unit $1/u$ and the pool width $\zeta$ (no sweep in the register); the tier map (its sweep is the default); a per-tier tokens-per-conversation factor and a clock alignment at local midnight (no source); a non-causal smoothing window and a load scenario per region pair (not built); $V_\ell$ as the whole block below the lease quantile (beyond the evaluation's memory budget); $V_\ell$ as a share of the mean lendable capacity (not defined); a uniform $\kappa$ multiplier (identical to the default).

sf_slack.text: Lendable slack (capacity minus the high-priority jobs' occupancy, at least 0) of the six GPU pools of Alibaba's cluster-trace-v2026-spot-gpu [duan2026gfs] at 5-min slots: daily minimum to maximum (band) and daily mean (line) over 177 days from the end of the trace's first week, which the analysis drops; each y axis runs from 0 to the pool's capacity (title). The trace's last 18 slots (90 min), in which every pool's slack jumps at once to at least 82% of its capacity, are left out. Thin light line: P25, the 25th percentile of the pool's slack over the whole series (the slack reaches it in at least 75% of the slots). At its default lease-size quantile (P25) the simulator takes this quantile of the slack left after the lender's notice buffer and rounds it down to whole layers, so the top of the block a spot lender offers lies at or below this line. (a) A10: P25 = 0; its slack is zero in 94.0% of the slots, in every slot until day 166, and its daily mean is 92–126 GPUs from day 167 on.
